final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger with UBS over the weekend as the dominant path, requiring a Federal Council emergency ordinance, CHF 9bn government guarantee, SNB liquidity facility of CHF 100bn+, and AT1 conversion to equity (rather than outright write-down) to minimize legal risk. Announcement must occur Sunday night before Asian markets open.
minority_objections: Standalone bridge with SNB liquidity and protective supervision mentioned as fallback if UBS deal collapses, but explicitly not the preferred path
key_conflicts: UBS demands maximum government guarantees and MAC protection vs. authorities wanting to minimize taxpayer exposure
AT1 bondholder treatment: full write-down saves CHF 16bn but creates high litigation risk vs. conversion-to-equity follows hierarchy but provides no savings
Federal Council political fragility with SVP and Greens/SP likely opposition requiring 4 of 7 votes
FINMA/SNB red line that SNB will not take credit risk without Federal guarantee
key_concessions: Federal Council to provide CHF 9bn first-loss guarantee on legacy Credit Suisse portfolios
FINMA to grant UBS 12-18 month regulatory capital relief and phase-in waiver
SNB to provide CHF 100bn+ liquidity facility with expanded collateral framework for troubled assets
Federal Council emergency ordinance to override competition law (COMCO) merger review
UBS to pay nominal price CHF 0.25-1.00/share (~90-97% discount) with CHF 1bn employee retention pool
Credit Suisse Chairman/CEO to resign as condition of deal
red_lines: UBS will not proceed without government guarantee - Board will vote no
UBS MAC clause: can reprice or withdraw if deposits fall >CHF 30bn over weekend
SNB will not take credit risk onto balance sheet without Federal guarantee
Announcement must occur Sunday night before Asian markets open to prevent Monday bank run
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Wealth client flight continuing post-announcement even from UBS if viewed as 'forced buyer of toxic bank'
International regulatory coordination (EU/US antitrust) treated as manageable but could create friction
Switzerland becoming a one-major-bank country with future moral hazard implications
Parliamentary ratification requirement for guarantee within 6 months creates political tail risk
downstream_risk_variables: Federal Council vote outcome (need 4 of 7) on Saturday evening
Actual deposit outflows Friday-to-Sunday vs. CHF 30bn MAC threshold
AT1 bondholder litigation success probability across multiple jurisdictions
UBS shareholder reaction to acquisition announcement
Effectiveness of Sunday night messaging to prevent Asian wealth client withdrawals Monday morning
uncertainty_notes: Final AT1 treatment remains a critical Saturday evening decision point between Federal Council, FINMA, and SNB - conversion-to-equity recommended but authorities may override for cost reasons if they believe full write-down is legally defensible. UBS Board final approval conditional on all terms being met. Federal Council political vote (4 of 7) is uncertain and requires intensive Saturday persuasion by Finance Minister.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Explicitly stated: 'government liquidity line will be read as life support - accelerating, not stopping, outflows' and 'Client confidence cannot be rebuilt incrementally'; standalone bridge is fallback only
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Entire recommendation structured around 'Forced Merger with UBS over the Weekend' with detailed timeline, term sheet, and execution steps; described as the dominant decision path
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 9bn Federal guarantee is binding constraint in term sheet; described as Tier 1 Decisive risk ('UBS will not bid without Federal loss protection'); SNB CHF 100bn facility required; emergency ordinance mandatory
marker_evidence.client_flight: Drives the weekend timeline constraint: '85%+ probability of Monday bank run if no deal'; 'Asian wealth clients begin Monday withdrawal instructions'; 'Intraday liquidity need could exceed CHF 50bn Monday alone'; forces Sunday night announcement
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Entire Section 2C devoted to AT1 treatment as Tier 1 Decisive risk; CHF 16bn at stake; three options analyzed; specific recommendation for conversion-to-equity at 1:100 ratio in term sheet; described as 'Critical Decision'
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Tier 1 Decisive risk: 'If authorities write down AT1 to zero while equity receives anything: Violates standard creditor hierarchy'; drives recommendation for conversion-to-equity rather than write-down; shapes Federal Council Saturday decision
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Tier 1 Decisive risk: 'Immediate legal challenges in multiple jurisdictions - Could freeze the transaction if court grants interim relief'; drives choice of Option 1 (conversion) over Option 2 (write-down): 'legal risk of full write-down is unacceptable for weekend timeline'
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Weekend timeline is the 'forcing function for the entire weekend'; detailed hour-by-hour schedule Friday-to-Sunday with hard deadlines; 'Saturday 1800: GO/NO-GO decision'; 'Sunday 2000: Federal Council ordinance'; emergency powers required to override standard timelines
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Tier 1 Decisive risk driving entire timeline: 'Weekend Execution Failure → Monday Bank Run' with '85%+ probability'; 'Asian wealth clients begin Monday withdrawal instructions'; 'Announcement must include named acquirer before Asian markets'; Sunday 2200 announcement deadline set explicitly
